correctness.rationale: The four image-shape cases are exhaustive for an order-preserving map from the complete height-two poset. They contribute respectively \(n(3^p-2^p)\), \(n(3^q-2^q)\), \(n2^q\), and \(n(2^p-2)\), summing to \(n(3^p+3^q-2)\). For \(n\ge3\), two distinct target minima have a common upper neighbor only when they are consecutive, and then that upper neighbor is unique; this is the only nontrivial crown incidence fact used. Every case gives a pointwise comparison with a constant map, hence a finite-space homotopy to a constant. An independent brute-force replay for \((p,q,n)=(2,2,3),(2,3,3),(3,2,3)\) recovered counts \(48,102,102\) and a comparable constant for every monotone map. The \(n=2\) sharp boundary is consistent with the rigidity of the four-point crown core.
residual_risks: The theorem is about direct finite-space maps, not maps after subdivision of the source.
